claim: The vasopressin type 2 receptor (V2R) is an essential G protein-coupled receptor (GPCR) in renal regulation of water homeostasis.
source: The vasopressin type 2 receptor (V2R) is an essential G protein-coupled receptor (GPCR) in renal regulation of water homeostasis.
evidence: This is a statement of established scientific knowledge about the V2R's physiological role.

claim: Upon stimulation, the V2R activates Gαs and Gαq/11.
source: Upon stimulation, the V2R activates Gαs and Gαq/11, which is followed by robust recruitment of β-arrestins and receptor internalization into endosomes.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data presented in the manuscript using mG protein recruitment assays and downstream signaling measurements.

claim: V2R stimulation is followed by robust recruitment of β-arrestins and receptor internalization into endosomes.
source: Upon stimulation, the V2R activates Gαs and Gαq/11, which is followed by robust recruitment of β-arrestins and receptor internalization into endosomes.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data showing β-arrestin recruitment kinetics and receptor internalization measurements.

claim: The β-arrestin association with the V2R does not terminate Gαs activation.
source: Unlike canonical GPCR signaling, the β-arrestin association with the V2R does not terminate Gαs activation, and thus, Gαs-mediated signaling is sustained while the receptor is internalized.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data showing sustained G protein activation in the presence of β-arrestins.

claim: Gαs-mediated signaling is sustained while the V2R is internalized.
source: Unlike canonical GPCR signaling, the β-arrestin association with the V2R does not terminate Gαs activation, and thus, Gαs-mediated signaling is sustained while the receptor is internalized.
evidence: This is demonstrated by kinetic measurements of G protein activation at endosomes shown in the figures.

claim: The V2R ability to co-interact with G protein/β-arrestin and promote endosomal G protein signaling is not restricted to Gαs, but also involves Gαq/11.
source: Here, we demonstrate that this V2R ability to co-interact with G protein/β-arrestin and promote endosomal G protein signaling is not restricted to Gαs, but also involves Gαq/11.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data using mGsq recruitment assays, DAG production measurements, and confocal microscopy.

claim: β-arrestins potentiate Gαs/Gαq/11 activation at endosomes rather than terminating their signaling.
source: Furthermore, our data imply that β-arrestins potentiate Gαs/Gαq/11 activation at endosomes rather than terminating their signaling.
evidence: This is inferred from transduction coefficient comparisons between V2R and V2β2AR, showing higher endosomal G protein activation for V2R which has stronger β-arrestin association.

claim: The V2R internalizes and promotes endosomal G protein activation independent of β-arrestins to a minor degree.
source: Surprisingly, we found that the V2R internalizes and promote endosomal G protein activation independent of β-arrestins to a minor degree.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data in Δβarr1/2 cells showing residual endosomal G protein activation and receptor internalization.

claim: Endosomal GPCR signaling can occur in both β-arrestin-dependent and -independent manners.
source: These new observations challenge the current model of endosomal GPCR signaling and suggest that this event can occur in both β-arrestin-dependent and -independent manners.
evidence: This is inferred from the observation of residual endosomal G protein activation in β-arrestin knockout cells.

claim: In the principal cells of the collecting duct, the V2R regulates water reabsorption from pre-urine by promoting translocation of water channel aquaporin 2 (AQP2) located in intracellular vesicles to the apical membrane (Nielsen et al., 1993).
source: Here, in the principal cells of the collecting duct, the V2R regulates water reabsorption from pre-urine by promoting translocation of water channel aquaporin 2 (AQP2) located in intracellular vesicles to the apical membrane (Nielsen et al., 1993).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous work.

claim: The net result of AQP2 translocation is an enhanced water permeability.
source: The net result of this translocation is an enhanced water permeability.
evidence: This is established knowledge about the physiological consequence of AQP2 translocation.

claim: Defective V2R signaling due to loss or gain of function mutations is associated with nephrogenic diabetes insipidus (Bichet and Bockenhauer, 2016).
source: Defective V2R signaling due to loss or gain of function mutations is associated with nephrogenic diabetes insipidus (Bichet and Bockenhauer, 2016) or nephrogenic syndrome of inappropriate antidiuresis (Carpentier et al., 2012), respectively.
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous work.

claim: Defective V2R signaling due to gain of function mutations is associated with nephrogenic syndrome of inappropriate antidiuresis (Carpentier et al., 2012).
source: Defective V2R signaling due to loss or gain of function mutations is associated with nephrogenic diabetes insipidus (Bichet and Bockenhauer, 2016) or nephrogenic syndrome of inappropriate antidiuresis (Carpentier et al., 2012), respectively.
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous work.

claim: The V2R belongs to the superfamily of G protein-coupled receptors (GPCRs).
source: The V2R belongs to the superfamily of G protein-coupled receptors (GPCRs), membrane proteins that control almost all physiological processes.
evidence: This is established knowledge about receptor classification.

claim: GPCRs are membrane proteins that control almost all physiological processes.
source: The V2R belongs to the superfamily of G protein-coupled receptors (GPCRs), membrane proteins that control almost all physiological processes.
evidence: This is established knowledge about GPCR function.

claim: Stimulation of GPCRs leads to coupling to and activation of heterotrimeric G proteins (Gαβγ), which initiates downstream signaling cascades that control global cellular responses.
source: Canonically, stimulation of GPCRs leads to coupling to and activation of heterotrimeric G proteins (Gαβγ), which initiates downstream signaling cascades that control global cellular responses.
evidence: This is established knowledge about canonical GPCR signaling.

claim: GPCRs can couple to four main families of Gα protein isoforms: Gαs/olf, Gαi/o, Gαq/11, and Gα12/13.
source: GPCRs can couple to four main families of Gα protein isoforms: Gαs/olf, Gαi/o, Gαq/11, and Gα12/13.
evidence: This is established knowledge about G protein families.

claim: Activation of each G protein family leads to distinct downstream signaling events and cell biological outcomes.
source: Activation of each family leads to distinct downstream signaling events and cell biological outcomes.
evidence: This is established knowledge about G protein signaling specificity.

claim: G protein activation is usually short lived and followed by receptor phosphorylation by GPCR kinases.
source: G protein activation is usually short lived and followed by receptor phosphorylation by GPCR kinases, which drives the recruitment of β-arrestins (βarrs) to the phosphorylated receptor.
evidence: This is established knowledge about canonical GPCR regulation.

claim: Receptor phosphorylation by GPCR kinases drives the recruitment of β-arrestins to the phosphorylated receptor.
source: G protein activation is usually short lived and followed by receptor phosphorylation by GPCR kinases, which drives the recruitment of β-arrestins (βarrs) to the phosphorylated receptor.
evidence: This is established knowledge about β-arrestin recruitment.

claim: β-arrestins interact with the same region of the receptor as G proteins, and their recruitment physically uncouples G proteins from the receptor which causes desensitization of G protein signaling (Pippig et al., 1993).
source: As βarrs interact with the same region of the receptor as G proteins, their recruitment physically uncouples G proteins from the receptor which causes desensitization of G protein signaling (Pippig et al., 1993).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous work.

claim: β-arrestins scaffold several proteins involved in endocytosis, which promotes receptor internalization into endosomes (Krupnick et al., 1997; Laporte et al., 1999).
source: In addition, βarrs scaffold several proteins involved in endocytosis, which promotes receptor internalization into endosomes (Krupnick et al., 1997; Laporte et al., 1999).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous work.

claim: Several GPCRs, including the V2R, have been reported to engage in G protein signaling after βarr-mediated receptor internalization into early endosomes and/or other intracellular compartments (Feinstein et al., 2013; Thomsen et al., 2016).
source: Several GPCRs, including the V2R, have been reported to engage in G protein signaling after βarr-mediated receptor internalization into early endosomes and/or other intracellular compartments (Feinstein et al., 2013; Thomsen et al., 2016).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous work.

claim: Some GPCRs, including the V2R, bind β-arrestins in a specific 'tail' conformation where β-arrestin only interacts with the phosphorylated receptor carboxy-terminal tail while the transmembrane core of the receptor remains unoccupied (Cahill et al., 2017; Shukla et al., 2014).
source: However, we discovered and delineated a new signaling paradigm whereby some GPCRs, including the V2R, bind βarrs in a specific manner; in this conformation, also called the 'tail' conformation, βarr only interacts with the phosphorylated receptor carboxy-terminal tail while the transmembrane core of the receptor remains unoccupied (Cahill et al., 2017; Shukla et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous work.

claim: β-arrestin in the tail conformation can promote certain β-arrestin-mediated functions such as receptor internalization and signaling (Cahill et al., 2017; Kumari et al., 2016; Kumari et al., 2017).
source: Interestingly, βarr in this tail conformation can promote certain βarr-mediated functions such as receptor internalization and signaling (Cahill et al., 2017; Kumari et al., 2016; Kumari et al., 2017).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous work.

claim: β-arrestin in the tail conformation does not desensitize G protein signaling because it does not compete for the receptor G protein-binding site (Cahill et al., 2017).
source: However, as βarr does not compete for the receptor G protein-binding site in this tail conformation, it does not desensitize G protein signaling (Cahill et al., 2017).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous work.

claim: The receptor in the tail conformation may interact simultaneously with G proteins and β-arrestin to form a GPCR–G protein–β-arrestin 'megaplex' (Cahill et al., 2017; Nguyen et al., 2019; Thomsen et al., 2016).
source: Rather, the receptor in this conformation may interact simultaneously with G proteins and βarr to form a GPCR–G protein–βarr 'megaplex' (Cahill et al., 2017; Nguyen et al., 2019; Thomsen et al., 2016).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous work.

claim: The simultaneous engagement with G protein and β-arrestin allows the receptor in megaplexes to maintain its ability to activate G protein signaling, even while being internalized into endosomes by β-arrestins.
source: Thus, the simultaneous engagement with G protein and βarr allows the receptor in these megaplexes to maintain its ability to activate G protein signaling, even while being internalized into endosomes by βarrs.
evidence: This is inferred from the structural and functional properties of megaplexes described in cited work.

claim: Endosomal Gαs signaling by V2R has been associated with enhanced and sustained translocation of AQP2 to the plasma membrane to facilitate water reabsorption (Feinstein et al., 2013).
source: Noteworthy, endosomal Gαs signaling by V2R has been associated with enhanced and sustained translocation of AQP2 to the plasma membrane to facilitate water reabsorption, and therefore, appears to play an important physiological role (Feinstein et al., 2013).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous work.

claim: Several studies report activation of the Gαq/11 isoforms by V2R (Avet et al., 2022; Heydenreich et al., 2022; Lykke et al., 2015; Zhu et al., 1994).
source: Although known as a Gαs-coupled receptor, several studies report activation of the Gαq/11 isoforms by V2R (Avet et al., 2022; Heydenreich et al., 2022; Lykke et al., 2015; Zhu et al., 1994) as well as unproductive coupling to Gα12 (Okashah et al., 2020).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous work.

claim: V2R shows unproductive coupling to Gα12 (Okashah et al., 2020).
source: Although known as a Gαs-coupled receptor, several studies report activation of the Gαq/11 isoforms by V2R (Avet et al., 2022; Heydenreich et al., 2022; Lykke et al., 2015; Zhu et al., 1994) as well as unproductive coupling to Gα12 (Okashah et al., 2020).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous work.

claim: Pulse-stimulation experiments of the V2R and parathyroid hormone type 1 receptor (PTHR) demonstrated that sustained Gαs-mediated signaling was enhanced by β-arrestin (Feinstein et al., 2011; Feinstein et al., 2013).
source: In addition, pulse-stimulation experiments of the V2R and parathyroid hormone type 1 receptor (PTHR) demonstrated that sustained Gαs-mediated signaling was enhanced by βarr (Feinstein et al., 2011; Feinstein et al., 2013).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous work.

claim: AVP treatment induced a rapid recruitment of mGs and mGsq but not mGsi nor mG12 to the plasma membrane.
source: In HEK293 cells expressing rGFP-CAAX, V2R, and similar levels of Rluc-fused mG proteins (Figure 1—figure supplement 1A), arginine vasopressin (AVP) treatment induced a rapid recruitment of mGs and mGsq but not mGsi nor mG12 to the plasma membrane.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1A.

claim: Maximal recruitment of mGs and mGsq to the plasma membrane were reached ~10 min after initial AVP stimulation.
source: Maximal recruitment of the mGs and mGsq were reached ~10 min after initial stimulation (Figure 1A, right panel).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1A.

claim: The V2R activates both Gαs and Gαq/11 at the plasma membrane.
source: These results suggest that the V2R activates both Gαs and Gαq/11 at the plasma membrane.
evidence: This is inferred from the mG protein recruitment data at the plasma membrane.

claim: AVP stimulation led to the recruitment of mGs and mGsq to early endosomes in cells expressing rGFP-Rab5.
source: In addition, AVP stimulation led to the recruitment of the same mG protein isoforms to early endosomes in cells expressing rGFP-Rab5, V2R, and similar levels of Rluc-fused mG proteins (Figure 1B, right panel, Figure 1—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1B.

claim: mGs and mGsq recruitment to early endosomes were slower and reached maximal levels 45–60 min after initial stimulation with AVP.
source: In contrast to the plasma membrane response, mGs and mGsq recruitment to early endosomes were slower and reached maximal levels 45–60 min after initial stimulation with AVP (Figure 1B, right panel).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1B.

claim: AVP induced a recruitment of Rluc-C1b at the plasma membrane, which confirms the production of DAG at the plasma membrane by V2R.
source: In line with the recruitment of mGsq at the plasma membrane observed in Figure 1A, AVP induced a recruitment of Rluc-C1b at the plasma membrane depicted by an increase of EbBRET values, which confirms the production of DAG at the plasma membrane by V2R (Figure 1C, right panel).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1C.

claim: The production of DAG at the plasma membrane by V2R is Gαq/11-dependent as a pre-treatment with YM254890 abrogated this downstream response.
source: Importantly, this production of DAG is Gαq/11-dependent as a pre-treatment with YM254890, an inhibitor of Gαq/11, abrogated this downstream response (Taniguchi et al., 2003).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data showing inhibition by YM254890 and a citation about the inhibitor.

claim: AVP induced a recruitment of Rluc-C1b to the early endosomal marker rGFP-Rab5, which suggests that DAG is produced at endosomal membranes.
source: Similar to the observed recruitment of mGsq to the early endosomes (Figure 1B), AVP also induced a recruitment of Rluc-C1b to the early endosomal marker rGFP-Rab5, which suggests that DAG is produced at endosomal membranes (Figure 1D, right panel).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1D.

claim: Endosomal DAG production was inhibited by YM254890 treatment, which demonstrates that it is Gαq/11 dependent.
source: This endosomal DAG production was also inhibited by YM254890 treatment, which demonstrates that it is Gαq/11 dependent (Figure 1D, right panel).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1D.

claim: AVP treatment induced phosphorylation of PKC in a Gαq/11-dependent fashion.
source: In line with the AVP-mediated production of DAG, AVP treatment also induced phosphorylation of PKC in a Gαq/11-dependent fashion (Figure 1E, right panel).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1E.

claim: In cells treated with AVP for 10 min, mGs and mGsq but not mGsi were redistributed along the periphery of the cells where they colocalized with Lck.
source: In contrast, in cells treated with AVP for 10 min, mGs and mGsq but not mGsi were redistributed along the periphery of the cells where they colocalized with Lck (Figure 2A, bottom panels, Figure 2B).
evidence: This is supported by confocal microscopy data shown in Figure 2A and 2B.

claim: Gαs and Gαq/11 are activated by the V2R at the plasma membrane.
source: These observations confirm that Gαs and Gαq/11 are activated by the V2R at the plasma membrane.
evidence: This is inferred from confocal microscopy showing colocalization of mGs and mGsq with plasma membrane marker.

claim: Robust colocalization between Halo-mGs, Halo-mGsq and RFP-EEA1 were found 45 min after initial AVP stimulation but not by vehicle treatment.
source: In cells expressing the early endosomal marker EEA1, robust colocalization between Halo-mGs, Halo-mGsq and RFP-EEA1 were found 45 min after initial AVP stimulation but not by vehicle treatment (Figure 2C, D).
evidence: This is supported by confocal microscopy data shown in Figure 2C and 2D.

claim: Gαs and Gαq/11 are activated by V2R first at plasma membrane, and later on, from early endosomes after the V2R has been internalized.
source: Together our EbBRET and confocal microscopy imaging data suggest that Gαs and Gαq/11 are activated by V2R first at plasma membrane, and later on, from early endosomes after the V2R has been internalized.
evidence: This is inferred from the combined EbBRET and confocal microscopy data showing temporal and spatial patterns of G protein activation.

claim: The V2R forms V2R-βarr-Gs megaplexes upon AVP stimulation (Thomsen et al., 2016).
source: As we already previously demonstrated that the V2R forms V2R-βarr-Gs megaplexes upon AVP stimulation (Thomsen et al., 2016), we here explored whether formation of such complexes potentially can be formed with Gq/11 as well.
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous work.

claim: The phosphorylated V2R carboxy-tail forms stable complexes with β-arrestin, whereas the carboxy-tail of the β2AR does not (Cahill et al., 2017).
source: We previously showed that the phosphorylated V2R carboxy-tail forms stable complexes with βarr, a requirement of megaplex formation, whereas the carboxy-tail of the β2AR does not (Cahill et al., 2017).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous work.

claim: Both the V2R and V2β2AR bind to AVP with similar affinities and activate adenylyl cyclase via Gαs with similar potencies (Oakley et al., 1999).
source: Both the V2R and V2β2AR bind to AVP with similar affinities and activate adenylyl cyclase via Gαs with similar potencies (Oakley et al., 1999).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous work.

claim: The V2β2AR activated both Gαs and Gαq, but not Gαi nor Gα12, at plasma membrane with a maximal response reached after ~10 min of stimulation.
source: Similar to the V2R, the V2β2AR activated both Gαs and Gαq, but not Gαi nor Gα12, at plasma membrane with a maximal response reached after ~10 min of stimulation (Figure 3A, Figure 3—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3A.

claim: β-arrestin rapidly dissociates from the V2β2AR shortly after its recruitment to the plasma membrane due to its low affinity for this receptor chimera (Oakley et al., 1999).
source: While the V2R and V2β2AR are both reported to internalize via a βarr-dependent mechanism, βarr has been reported to rapidly dissociate from the V2β2AR shortly after its recruitment to the plasma membrane due to its low affinity for this receptor chimera (Oakley et al., 1999).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous work.

claim: β-arrestin stays associated with the V2R during its internalization into endosomes owing to its high affinity for the V2R (Oakley et al., 1999).
source: In contrast, βarr stays associated with the V2R during its internalization into endosomes owning to its high affinity for the V2R (Oakley et al., 1999).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous work.

claim: Both V2R and V2β2AR recruited βarr1 and βarr2 at plasma membrane maximally after 10 min of stimulation with AVP.
source: At similar levels of receptor and βarr expressions (Figure 3—figure supplement 2), both receptors recruited βarr1 and βarr2 at plasma membrane maximally after 10 min of stimulation with AVP (Figure 3B, right upper panel).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3B.

claim: The presence of β-arrestins at the plasma membrane declined rapidly after 10 min in V2R-expressing cells, while remaining for longer periods of time in V2β2AR-expressing cells.
source: However, the presence of βarrs at the plasma membrane declined rapidly hereafter 10 min in V2R-expressing cells, while remaining for longer periods of time in V2β2AR-expressing cells.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3B.

claim: The translocation of β-arrestins to the plasma membrane was more robust for the V2R as compared to the V2β2AR, which is reminiscent from the higher affinity of β-arrestins for the V2R as compared to the β2AR (Oakley et al., 2000).
source: Additionally, the translocation of βarrs to the plasma membrane was more robust for the V2R as compared to the V2β2AR, which is reminiscent from the higher affinity of βarrs for the V2R as compared to theβ2AR (Oakley et al., 2000).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data and a citation to previous work.

claim: AVP treatment induced a robust but slower enrichment of β-arrestins to early endosomes with V2R reaching a maximal response after approximately 45 min of stimulation.
source: In contrast to the rapid translocation of βarrs to the plasma membrane, AVP treatment induced a robust but slower enrichment of βarrs to early endosomes with V2R reaching a maximal response after approximately 45 min of stimulation (Figure 3B, right bottom panel).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3B.

claim: AVP stimulation of V2β2AR did not result in β-arrestin translocation to early endosomes.
source: Importantly, as opposed to V2R, AVP stimulation of V2β2AR did not result in βarr translocation to early endosomes (Figure 3B, right bottom panel).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3B.

claim: Bright luminescence signals involving mGs/βarr1 and mGsq/βarr1 were detected upon stimulation of the V2R but not the V2β2AR.
source: Using this approach, we detected bright luminescence signals involving mGs/βarr1 (Figure 3C, upper right panel) and mGsq/βarr1 (Figure 3C, bottom right panel) upon stimulation of the V2R but not the V2β2AR.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3C.

claim: The dual coupling of Gαq/11/βarr to V2R appeared to be faster than the co-coupling of Gαs/βarr.
source: Interestingly, the dual coupling of Gαq/11/βarr to V2R appeared to be faster than the co-coupling of Gαs/βarr.
evidence: This is inferred from the kinetic data shown in Figure 3C.

claim: 20 min was required to reach the maximal response of V2R-stimulated mGs/βarr1 co-coupling.
source: While 20 min was required to reach the maximal response of V2R-stimulated mGs/βarr1 co-coupling, 8 min was sufficient to obtain the maximal levels of mGsq/βarr1 recruitment to the V2R (Figure 3C, right panels).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3C.

claim: 8 min was sufficient to obtain the maximal levels of mGsq/βarr1 recruitment to the V2R.
source: While 20 min was required to reach the maximal response of V2R-stimulated mGs/βarr1 co-coupling, 8 min was sufficient to obtain the maximal levels of mGsq/βarr1 recruitment to the V2R (Figure 3C, right panels).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3C.

claim: After prolonged stimulation of V2R with AVP, around 75% of βarr2 colocalized with mGs in endocytic vesicles.
source: However, after prolonged stimulation of V2R with AVP, around 75% of βarr2 colocalized with mGs in endocytic vesicles (Figure 3D, F).
evidence: This is supported by confocal microscopy data shown in Figure 3D and 3F.

claim: In V2β2AR-stimulated cells, little to no colocalization was observed between βarr2 and mGs upon prolonged stimulation with AVP.
source: In V2β2AR-stimulated cells, little to no colocalization was observed between βarr2 and mGs upon prolonged stimulation with AVP (Figure 3D, F).
evidence: This is supported by confocal microscopy data shown in Figure 3D and 3F.

claim: In V2β2AR-expressing cells around 75% of the intracellular mGs clusters do not colocalize with βarr2.
source: As opposed to V2R-expressing cells for which nearly all the clusters of intracellular mGs colocalize with βarr2, in V2β2AR-expressing cells around 75% of the intracellular mGs clusters do not colocalize with βarr2 (Figure 3G).
evidence: This is supported by confocal microscopy data shown in Figure 3G.

claim: The results suggest simultaneous coupling of Gαs/βarr2 to the V2R in endosomes but not to the V2β2AR.
source: These results suggest simultaneous coupling of Gαs/βarr2 to the V2R in endosomes but not to the V2β2AR.
evidence: This is inferred from the colocalization data showing mGs and βarr2 together in V2R-expressing cells but not V2β2AR-expressing cells.

claim: Upon AVP stimulation, approximately 75% of βarr2 colocalized with mGsq in intracellular vesicles in V2R-expressing cells, whereas poor colocalization was observed in V2β2AR-expressing cells.
source: Upon AVP stimulation, approximately 75% of βarr2 colocalized with mGsq in intracellular vesicles in V2R-expressing cells, whereas poor colocalization was observed in V2β2AR-expressing cells (Figure 3E, F).
evidence: This is supported by confocal microscopy data shown in Figure 3E and 3F.

claim: Clear clusters of intracellular mGsq were visible in cells expressing V2β2AR.
source: Similar to cells expressing mGs, clear clusters of intracellular mGsq were visible in cells expressing V2β2AR (Figure 3E, G), suggesting a certain level of endosomal Gαs/Gαq signaling despite the absence of βarr2.
evidence: This is supported by confocal microscopy data shown in Figure 3E and 3G.

claim: There is a certain level of endosomal Gαs/Gαq signaling despite the absence of βarr2.
source: Similar to cells expressing mGs, clear clusters of intracellular mGsq were visible in cells expressing V2β2AR (Figure 3E, G), suggesting a certain level of endosomal Gαs/Gαq signaling despite the absence of βarr2.
evidence: This is inferred from the observation of intracellular mGsq clusters in V2β2AR-expressing cells where βarr2 is not present at endosomes.

claim: A robust decrease in the ability of the V2R to activate Gαs and Gαq at endosomes was observed in Δβarr1/2 cells as compared to their parental counterpart.
source: In contrast to Gαs and Gαq/11 activation at the plasma membrane, which were not negatively affected by the absence of βarrs (Figure 4A, Table 1), we observed a robust decrease in the ability of the V2R to activate Gαs and Gαq at endosomes in Δβarr1/2 cells as compared to their parental counterpart (Figure 4B, Table 1).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4B and Table 1.

claim: Gαs and Gαq/11 activation at the plasma membrane were not negatively affected by the absence of β-arrestins.
source: In contrast to Gαs and Gαq/11 activation at the plasma membrane, which were not negatively affected by the absence of βarrs (Figure 4A, Table 1), we observed a robust decrease in the ability of the V2R to activate Gαs and Gαq at endosomes in Δβarr1/2 cells as compared to their parental counterpart (Figure 4B, Table 1).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4A and Table 1.

claim: β-arrestins play an important role in endosomal Gαs/Gαq/11 activation by the V2R.
source: These data demonstrate the important role of βarrs in endosomal Gαs/Gαq/11 activation by the V2R.
evidence: This is inferred from the reduced endosomal G protein activation in β-arrestin knockout cells.

claim: Significant residual G protein activation from endosomes was observed in Δβarr1/2 cells.
source: However, although the Δβarr1/2 cells do not express βarrs, we still observed significant residual G protein activation from endosomes.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4B.

claim: The V2R internalizes into endosomes to some extent in a β-arrestin-independent manner from where G proteins are stimulated.
source: This surprising observation suggests that the V2R internalizes into endosomes to some extent in a βarr-independent manner from where G proteins are stimulated.
evidence: This is inferred from the observation of residual endosomal G protein activation in β-arrestin knockout cells.

claim: AVP stimulation of the V2R-Rluc led to a robust decrease of EbBRET values in parental HEK293 cells, which indicates strong receptor internalization.
source: In parental HEK293 cells, AVP stimulation of the V2R-Rluc led to a robust decrease of EbBRET values, which indicates strong receptor internalization (Figure 4C, right panel).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4C.

claim: Significant internalization of the V2R was observed in Δβarr1/2 HEK293 cells, although less than in the parental cells.
source: Interestingly, we also observed significant internalization of the V2R in Δβarr1/2 HEK293 cells, although less than in the parental cells (Figure 4C, right panel).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4C.

claim: A minor population of V2R internalizes independently of β-arrestins and contributes to endosomal Gαs and Gαq/11 signaling.
source: These results suggest that a minor population of V2R internalizes independently of βarrs and contributes to endosomal Gαs and Gαq/11 signaling.
evidence: This is inferred from the observation of V2R internalization and endosomal G protein activation in β-arrestin knockout cells.

claim: β-arrestins directly potentiate G protein activation by the V2R in early endosomes.
source: In the current study, we show that βarrs directly potentiate G protein activation by the V2R in early endosomes (Figure 4D).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data showing higher transduction coefficients for V2R compared to V2β2AR at endosomes.

claim: The transduction coefficients of Gαs activation at the plasma membrane were similar for the V2R and V2β2AR, but higher for the V2R than V2β2AR in early endosomes.
source: In cells expressing mGs, the transduction coefficients of Gαs activation at the plasma membrane were similar for the V2R and V2β2AR, but higher for the V2R than V2β2AR in early endosomes (Figure 4D, left panel, Table 2).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4D and Table 2.

claim: The transduction coefficients of Gαq/11 activation at the plasma membrane were similar for the V2R and V2β2AR, but higher for the V2R than V2β2AR in early endosomes.
source: Similarly, in cells expressing mGsq, the transduction coefficients of Gαq/11 activation at the plasma membrane were similar for the V2R and V2β2AR, but higher for the V2R than V2β2AR in early endosomes (Figure 4D, right panel, Table 2).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4D and Table 2.

claim: β-arrestins potentiate activation of G proteins by the V2R in early endosomes.
source: Altogether these results indicate that βarrs potentiate activation of G proteins by the V2R in early endosomes.
evidence: This is inferred from the transduction coefficient data comparing V2R and V2β2AR.

claim: Both Gαs and Gαq/11 are activated by the V2R at the plasma membrane and early endosomes.
source: Here, we demonstrated that both Gαs and Gαq/11 are activated by the V2R at the plasma membrane and early endosomes using a mG protein-based approach as well as biosensors of downstream signaling.
evidence: This is supported by multiple experimental approaches including mG protein recruitment, DAG production, and PKC activation assays.

claim: The mG protein-based approach measures the receptor's ability to couple to G proteins in real time rather than G protein-mediated signaling outputs.
source: The mG protein-based approach measures the receptor's ability to couple to G proteins in real time rather than G protein-mediated signaling outputs.
evidence: This is a description of the methodological approach used in the study.

claim: The PTHR couples to both Gαs and Gαq/11 (Schwindinger et al., 1998).
source: The PTHR, a GPCR that regulates mineral ion homeostasis and bone development, also couples to both Gαs and Gαq/11 (Schwindinger et al., 1998).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous work.

claim: The reduction of PTHR internalization by βarr1 and βarr2 depletion strongly decreases endosomal Gαs/cAMP signaling.
source: Similar to our observations of the V2R, the reduction of PTHR internalization by βarr1 and βarr2 depletion strongly decreases endosomal Gαs/cAMP signaling.
evidence: This is stated as a comparison to the V2R findings, drawing on established knowledge about PTHR.

claim: β-arrestin-mediated receptor internalization shuts down Gαq/11-mediated responses for the PTHR (Castro et al., 2002; Feinstein et al., 2011).
source: However, in contrast to the V2R, βarr-mediated receptor internalization shuts down Gαq/11-mediated responses, and thus, the PTHR does not appear to stimulate Gαq/11 from endosomes (Castro et al., 2002; Feinstein et al., 2011).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous work.

claim: Multiple laboratories have reported endosomal GPCR signaling events downstream of Gαq/11 activation (Gorvin et al., 2018; Jensen et al., 2017; Jimenez-Vargas et al., 2018).
source: However, it is unlikely to be a general feature of these G protein isoforms as multiple laboratories have reported endosomal GPCR signaling events downstream of Gαq/11 activation (Gorvin et al., 2018; Jensen et al., 2017; Jimenez-Vargas et al., 2018).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous work.

claim: Wright et al. demonstrated that stimulation of Gαq/11 protein isoforms by receptors at the plasma membrane does not necessarily lead to the activation of the exact same isoforms at endosomes (Wright et al., 2021).
source: Recently, direct activation of Gαq/11 from early endosomes was monitored using a mG protein-based approach and effector membrane translocation assay (EMTA). In this study, Wright et al. demonstrated that stimulation of Gαq/11 protein isoforms by receptors at the plasma membrane does not necessarily lead to the activation of the exact same isoforms at endosomes (Wright et al., 2021).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous work.

claim: The thromboxane A2 alpha isoform receptor (TPαR) robustly activates all the Gαq/11 isoforms (Gαq, Gα11, Gα14, and Gα15) at the plasma membrane, but only activates Gαq and Gα11 isoforms at endosomes.
source: For example, the authors showed that the thromboxane A2 alpha isoform receptor (TPαR) robustly activates all the Gαq/11 isoforms (Gαq, Gα11, Gα14, and Gα15) at the plasma membrane, but only activates Gαq and Gα11 isoforms at endosomes.
evidence: This is cited from Wright et al., 2021 as an example of differential G protein isoform activation.

claim: The muscarinic acetylcholine M3 receptor (M3R) activates all four Gαq/11 isoforms both at plasma membrane and endosomes.
source: In contrast, the muscarinic acetylcholine M3 receptor (M3R) activates all four Gαq/11 isoforms both at plasma membrane and endosomes.
evidence: This is cited from Wright et al., 2021 as an example of consistent G protein isoform activation.

claim: G protein selectivity at plasma membrane is mainly dependent on receptor conformation (Rose et al., 2014; Van Eps et al., 2018), specific residues present at the GPCR–Gα protein interface (Flock et al., 2017) as well as the location and duration of these intermolecular interactions (Sandhu et al., 2022).
source: While G protein selectivity at plasma membrane is mainly dependent on receptor conformation (Rose et al., 2014; Van Eps et al., 2018), specific residues present at the GPCR–Gα protein interface (Flock et al., 2017) as well as the location and duration of these intermolecular interactions (Sandhu et al., 2022), endosomal G protein activation seems to be controlled by additional factors that are not fully understood.
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous work.

claim: Endosomal G protein activation seems to be controlled by additional factors that are not fully understood.
source: While G protein selectivity at plasma membrane is mainly dependent on receptor conformation (Rose et al., 2014; Van Eps et al., 2018), specific residues present at the GPCR–Gα protein interface (Flock et al., 2017) as well as the location and duration of these intermolecular interactions (Sandhu et al., 2022), endosomal G protein activation seems to be controlled by additional factors that are not fully understood.
evidence: This is inferred from the observation that endosomal G protein selectivity differs from plasma membrane selectivity.

claim: Class A GPCRs such as the β2AR are defined by harboring few single phosphorylation sites, which form interactions with positively charged residues of β-arrestins (Shukla et al., 2013).
source: Class A GPCRs such as the β2AR are defined by harboring few single phosphorylation sites, which form interactions with positively charged residues of βarrs (Shukla et al., 2013).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous work.

claim: The class A GPCR–β-arrestin association depends on an interaction between the β-arrestin fingerloop region and the receptor transmembrane core, which sterically block G protein access to the GPCR (Cahill et al., 2017; Shukla et al., 2014).
source: In addition to the phosphorylated receptor residues, the class A GPCR–βarr association also depends on an interaction between the βarr fingerloop region and the receptor transmembrane core, which sterically block G protein access to the GPCR (Cahill et al., 2017; Shukla et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous work.

claim: The class A GPCR–β-arrestin association is transient and the complex dissociates shortly after endocytosis, which results in receptor recycling back to the cell surface.
source: The class A GPCR–βarr association is transient and the complex dissociates shortly after endocytosis, which results in receptor recycling back to the cell surface.
evidence: This is established knowledge about class A GPCR trafficking.

claim: Class B GPCRs including the V2R are defined by having phosphorylation site clusters in the carboxy-terminal tail that form highly stable associations with β-arrestins solely through this region.
source: In contrast, class B GPCRs including the V2R are defined by having phosphorylation site clusters in the carboxy-terminal tail that form highly stable associations with βarrs solely through this region.
evidence: This is established knowledge about class B GPCR characteristics.

claim: The strong interaction between class B GPCRs and β-arrestins leads to prolonged receptor internalization into endosomes (Cahill et al., 2017).
source: This strong interaction leads to prolonged receptor internalization into endosomes (Cahill et al., 2017).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous work.

claim: The stability of the GPCR–β-arrestin complex 'tail' conformation does not depend on the interaction between the β-arrestin fingerloop region and the receptor core.
source: As the stability of this GPCR–βarr complex 'tail' conformation does not depend on the interaction between the βarr fingerloop region and the receptor core, the GPCR can interact simultaneously with G proteins to forms a GPCR–G protein–βarr megaplex (Nguyen et al., 2019; Thomsen et al., 2016).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous work.

claim: Receptors in megaplexes can internalize via β-arrestins into different intracellular compartments while stimulating G protein signaling for prolonged periods of time (Cahill et al., 2017; Calebiro et al., 2009; Feinstein et al., 2013; Ferrandon et al., 2009; Thomsen et al., 2016).
source: As the receptors in these megaplexes maintain their ability to activate G proteins, they can internalize via βarrs into different intracellular compartments while stimulating G protein signaling for prolonged periods of time (Cahill et al., 2017; Calebiro et al., 2009; Feinstein et al., 2013; Ferrandon et al., 2009; Thomsen et al., 2016).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous work.

claim: Formation of megaplexes at intracellular compartments has previously only been reported involving Gαs or Gαi/o proteins (Hahn et al., 2022; Smith et al., 2021; Thomsen et al., 2016).
source: Previously, formation of megaplexes at intracellular compartments has only been reported involving Gαs or Gαi/o proteins (Hahn et al., 2022; Smith et al., 2021; Thomsen et al., 2016).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous work.

claim: Megaplex formation is not confined to Gαs or Gαi/o proteins but also appears to form with other G protein isoforms such as Gαq/11.
source: In the present study, we demonstrate that megaplex formation is not confined to these G protein isoforms but also appears to form with other G protein isoforms such as Gαq/11.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data showing simultaneous recruitment of mGsq and β-arrestins.

claim: Feinstein et al. previously demonstrated that V2R-stimulated G protein activation is positively modulated by the presence of βarr2 (Feinstein et al., 2013).
source: These findings are further supported by Feinstein et al. who previously demonstrated that V2R-stimulated G protein activation is positively modulated by the presence of βarr2 (Feinstein et al., 2013).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous work.

claim: In the recent cryo-electron microscopy high-resolution structure of an engineered class B GPCR–Gs–βarr1 megaplex, no direct interaction between the heterotrimeric Gs and βarr1 was observed (Nguyen et al., 2019).
source: However, in the recent cryo-electron microscopy high-resolution structure of an engineered class B GPCR–Gs–βarr1 megaplex, no direct interaction between the heterotrimeric Gs and βarr1 was observed, and thus, it is not obvious how βarrs may affect G protein activity from this structure (Nguyen et al., 2019).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous work.

claim: Biochemical studies of the megaplex and G protein–β-arrestins interactions demonstrated that β-arrestin can serve as a scaffold for the Gβγ subunits that are released upon activation of the heterotrimeric G protein (Thomsen et al., 2016; Wehbi et al., 2013; Yang et al., 2009).
source: On the other hand, biochemical studies of the megaplex and G protein–βarrs interactions demonstrated that βarr can serve as a scaffold for the Gβγ subunits that are released upon activation of the heterotrimeric G protein (Thomsen et al., 2016; Wehbi et al., 2013; Yang et al., 2009).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous work.

claim: The Gβγ scaffolding role of β-arrestin may confine Gαs and Gαq/11 near endosomally located V2R, leading to their re-activation as soon as the inactive GDP-bound Gα with Gβγ subunits reassemble.
source: Thus, this Gβγ scaffolding role of βarr may confine Gαs and Gαq/11 near endosomally located V2R, leading to their re-activation as soon as the inactive GDP-bound Gα with Gβγ subunits reassemble.
evidence: This is a speculative mechanism proposed to explain how β-arrestins potentiate endosomal G protein activation.

claim: The results of the Gβγ scaffolding mechanism would be a net increase in the G protein activation rate.
source: The results of such activation mechanism would be a net increase in the G protein activation rate.
evidence: This is inferred as a consequence of the proposed Gβγ scaffolding mechanism.

claim: Despite the GPCR–βarr coupling being fully functional and the fusion 'complex' internalizing constitutively, the receptor maintains its ability to activate G proteins upon agonist stimulation.
source: We showed that despite the GPCR–βarr coupling being fully functional and this fusion 'complex' internalizing constitutively, the receptor maintains its ability to activate G proteins upon agonist stimulation (Nguyen et al., 2019; Thomsen et al., 2016).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous work using GPCR-β-arrestin fusion constructs.

claim: For some receptors such as the apelin receptor β-arrestin association is not required for clathrin-mediated internalization (Pope et al., 2016).
source: For some receptors such as the apelin receptor βarr association is not required for clathrin-mediated internalization (Pope et al., 2016).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous work.

claim: Several GPCRs internalize independently of any clathrin and β-arrestin associations via caveolae or by fast endophilin-mediated endocytosis (Moo et al., 2021).
source: Alternatively, several GPCRs also internalize independently of any clathrin and βarr associations via caveolae or by fast endophilin-mediated endocytosis (Moo et al., 2021).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous work.

claim: The glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor (GLP1R) internalizes in a β-arrestin-independent manner and signals via Gαs from endosomes to promote glucose-stimulated insulin secretion in pancreatic β cells (Claing et al., 2000; Kuna et al., 2013).
source: Notably, the glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor (GLP1R) internalizes in a βarr-independent manner and signals via Gαs from endosomes to promote glucose-stimulated insulin secretion in pancreatic β cells, which highlights the physiological relevance of βarr-independent endosomal G protein signaling (Claing et al., 2000; Kuna et al., 2013).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous work.

claim: VIPR1 promotes robust G protein signaling from endosomes in a completely β-arrestin-independent fashion (Blythe and von Zastrow, 2023).
source: Interestingly, in a very recent study of the vasoactive intestinal peptide receptor 1 (VIPR1) by Blythe and von Zastrow, it was shown that VIPR1 promotes robust G protein signaling from endosomes and that this occurs in a completely βarr-independent fashion (Blythe and von Zastrow, 2023).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous work.

claim: Agonist stimulation of VIPR1 led to recruitment of βarr1 and receptor internalization into endosomes where VIPR1 and βarr1 colocalized.
source: Surprisingly, the authors observed that agonist stimulation of VIPR1 led to recruitment of βarr1 and receptor internalization into endosomes where VIPR1 and βarr1 colocalized.
evidence: This is cited from Blythe and von Zastrow, 2023.

claim: Despite the potential interaction between VIPR1 and β-arrestins, the presence of βarr1/2 had little to no effect on receptor internalization and the ability of VIPR1 to activate G protein from endosomes (Blythe and von Zastrow, 2023).
source: However, despite this potential interaction between VIPR1 and βarrs, the presence of βarr1/2 had little to no effect on receptor internalization and the ability of VIPR1 to activate G protein from endosomes (Blythe and von Zastrow, 2023).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous work.

claim: β-arrestin-independent endosomal G protein signaling likely represents a more general mechanism that is utilized by multiple GPCRs to regulate important physiological functions.
source: As three independent studies using two different receptor systems now have found that endosomal G protein signaling can be achieved independent of βarrs, it is likely that this alternative mode of signaling represents a more general mechanism that is utilized by multiple GPCRs to regulate important physiological functions.
evidence: This is inferred from the observation of β-arrestin-independent endosomal signaling in multiple receptor systems.

claim: V2R-mediated endosomal G protein activation is not restricted to the Gαs isoform but also occurs with the Gαq/11 isoforms.
source: We demonstrated that V2R-mediated endosomal G protein activation is not restricted to the Gαs isoform but also occurs with the Gαq/11 isoforms.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data showing mGsq recruitment and DAG production at endosomes.

claim: A major part of V2R endosomal G protein activation is β-arrestin-dependent, and presumably takes place through the formation of V2R–G protein–β-arrestin megaplexes.
source: A major part of this endosomal G protein activation is βarr-dependent, and presumably takes place through the formation of V2R–G protein–βarr megaplexes.
evidence: This is inferred from the reduced endosomal G protein activation in β-arrestin knockout cells and the observation of simultaneous G protein and β-arrestin recruitment.

claim: The presence of β-arrestins in megaplexes potentiates the ability of the V2R to activate G protein within endosomes.
source: Interestingly, the presence of βarrs in these megaplexes potentiates the ability of the V2R to activate G protein within endosomes.
evidence: This is supported by transduction coefficient data comparing V2R and V2β2AR.

claim: V2R-mediated endosomal G protein activation can take place in a completely β-arrestin-independent fashion.
source: Surprisingly, we found that this mechanism is not the only way internalized V2R stimulates G protein signaling from endosomes since this event can take place in a completely βarr-independent fashion as well.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data showing residual endosomal G protein activation in β-arrestin knockout cells.

claim: The mechanism of β-arrestin-independent endosomal G protein activation by the V2R might represent a general aspect of GPCR biology that control important physiological and pathophysiological processes.
source: However, since similar observations were made of other GPCRs including the GLP1R and VIPR1, the mechanism might represent a general aspect of GPCR biology that control important physiological and pathophysiological processes.
evidence: This is speculated based on the observation of similar phenomena in multiple receptor systems.

claim: At the plasma membrane, AVP binding to V2R results in receptor-mediated Gαs or Gαq activation.
source: At the plasma membrane, arginine vasopressin (AVP) binding to V2R results in receptor-mediated Gαs or Gαq activation.
evidence: This is depicted in Figure 5 and supported by experimental data throughout the manuscript.

claim: Initial G protein activation at the plasma membrane is followed by V2R internalization into early endosomes.
source: This initial G protein activation at the plasma membrane is followed by V2R internalization into early endosomes.
evidence: This is depicted in Figure 5 and supported by experimental data showing temporal progression of signaling.

claim: V2R internalization occurs primarily in a β-arrestin-dependent manner, leading to the formation of a megaplex with Gαs or Gαq/11 and robust activation of these G proteins from endosomes.
source: This internalization occurs primarily in a βarr-dependent manner, leading to the formation of a megaplex with Gαs or Gαq/11 and robust activation of these G proteins from endosomes.
evidence: This is depicted in Figure 5 and supported by experimental data showing reduced endosomal signaling in β-arrestin knockout cells.

claim: A minor population of V2R internalize in a β-arrestin-independent fashion, which also leads to minor but significant Gαs or Gαq/11 activation from endosomes.
source: Additionally, a minor population of V2R internalize in a βarr-independent fashion, which also leads to minor but significant Gαs or Gαq/11 activation from endosomes.
evidence: This is depicted in Figure 5 and supported by experimental data showing residual endosomal signaling in β-arrestin knockout cells.
